verdict.label: Worth checking
verdict.headline: Almagreira Lunch
verdict.reason: Almagreira is worth a quick check for lunch, but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  The wind should be manageable, but not a big advantage.  The tide and timing are lining up well for this spot.

conversationalSummary.text: TODAY I’d go check the cams first, because Almagreira at lunch is the best option but it’s a bit of a rare, small-window kind of day. Even though the tide’s mid rising, the wind is mixed and those bigger gusts could make it messy fast. Surfline consistency looks poor, so I’d only leave if Surfline or MEO Beachcam looks noticeably cleaner than expected. If they don’t, I’d probably save the drive.

best.explanation: Almagreira looks like a small north coast window for Rare window, Low confidence: 0.3-0.6 m, 27 kJ, 6 s period, lully 0/100, and wind is not fully clear.  An exposed north-coast beach break with more raw swell than Baleal; this is best for small, clean north-coast days when protected spots look underpowered; 6-9s at mid tide can make exposed beaches like Belgas / Almagreira / Cerro / Meio da Baia sharp and rippable, so checking exposed beaches makes sense.  Watch: Surfline consistency is lully; gusts over 35 km/h could make it messy.

ranked.explanation: Cerro looks like a fun-sized window for Too soft, Medium confidence: 0.6-0.9 m, 45 kJ, 7 s period, lully 6/100, and wind is not fully clear.  A sheltered beachbreak with gentle lefts and rights, somewhat similar to Cantinho but less consistent; this is best for manageable bodyboard waves when north-northwest swell reaches the bay with clean southerly wind; 6-9s at mid tide can make exposed beaches like Belgas / Almagreira / Cerro / Meio da Baia sharp and rippable; worth keeping on the radar because Surfline is showing it above Poor while most other local spots are Poor..  Watch: Surfline consistency is lully; Cerro may feel too soft without more push.
